question.leadin: This politically-motivated event was perpetrated by activists who exited the Old South Meeting House dressed as Native Americans.
question.text: Name this event in which a group of rebellious colonists dumped over 300 chests of a certain British good into a Massachusetts harbor.
question.clue: A comment made by Samuel Adams allegedly triggered the beginning of this event.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the kids television series Liberty's Kids.
swap.text: This American general appeared in multiple episodes of Liberty's Kids, the first of which involved disagreement between him and Ethan Allen, when they co-led the capture of Fort Ticonderoga in 1775.
swap.clue: This general made an arduous 1775 march through Maine to join Richard Montgomery in attacking Quebec City, where his leg was shattered.

question.leadin: Named for the Chancellor of the Exchequer who proposed them, they were repealed on March 5, 1770, the same day as a notable snowball fight in Massachusetts.
question.text: Name these Acts of Parliament, designed to pay for British war debts following the Seven Years' War.
question.clue: The "Massachusetts Circular" letter was written by Samuel Adams in response to this program, and these acts led to the seizure of a sloop owned by John Hancock, the Liberty.

swap.text: de Gouges' Declaration of the Rights of Woman was a response to the Declaration of the Rights of Man, a 1789 document written in part by this French general, who had spent several years in America fighting for the colonists.
swap.answerHtml: Marquis de Lafayette (accept Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier)
swap.clue: With the Comte de Mirabeau, this man drafted the Declaration of the Rights of Man, which was modeled after the Declaration of Independence.

question.leadin: This general's namesake administrative code gave British people higher status in India than native inhabitants.
question.text: Name this Governor-General of India, who had earlier surrendered to George Washington at Yorktown.
question.clue: In another war, he served under General William Howe during the campaigns for New York City and Philadelphia, and he later defeated the army of Horatio Gates at the Battle of Camden.

swap.text: This Founding Father was the first postmaster general and the primary author of Poor Richard's Almanack.
swap.clue: He served on the Committee of Five and indirectly prompted Louis XVI to sign the Edict of Versailles while an ambassador.

question.text: This colonial governor of Massachusetts evacuated soldiers to Castle Island after the massacre. Colonists published letters written by this governor that allegedly showed his intent to deprive colonists of their rights.
question.clue: For actually leaking this politician's letters, Benjamin Franklin was removed from his office as Postmaster General, although the public fixated on this administrator's suggestion to abridge "English liberties."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about women who helped the US win wars, each in their own ways.
swap.text: This woman fought at the Battle of Monmouth during the Revolutionary War. According to legend, her husband William collapsed during the battle, and she took his place manning artillery.
swap.clue: This possibly-legendary woman took her husband's place loading cannons at the Battle of Monmouth during the American Revolution. Her nickname comes from her previous role as a water carrier.

question.text: Following Horatio Gates' defeat at the Battle of Camden, this man became commander of the army of the south, where he won the battle of Eutaw Springs. For 15 points, name this general whose victory at Guilford Courthouse forced Cornwallis to retreat to Yorktown.
question.clue: While working for this person's widow at the Mulberry Grove plantation outside Savannah, Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin.

swap.leadin: Name these battles featuring George Washington.
swap.text: This battle of late June, 1778 saw Washington attack the troops of Sir Henry Clinton near modern-day Freehold, New Jersey. It's more famous for the actions of Molly Pitcher.
swap.clue: This battle ended the Philadelphia campaign, as Henry Clinton was commanded to evacuate to New York.

question.leadin: Prior to this battle, Nathanael Greene split his army, sending a Daniel Morgan-led contingent into British supply lines.
question.text: Name this January 17th, 1781 battle in which Daniel Morgan scored a decisive victory over a British force led by Banastre Tarleton. Along with the earlier Battle of King's Mountain, it turned the tide in the Southern theater.
question.clue: The victorious general at this battle ordered his first two lines of untrained troops to fire at enemy officers before retreating behind a third line of Maryland, Virginia and Delaware veterans.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about naval engagements in the American Revolution.
swap.text: This so-called Father of the American Navy and captain of the Bonhomme Richard forced the HMS Serapis to surrender.
swap.clue: This naval commander raided English coastal towns during the American Revolution, and defeated the British sloop HMS Drake in 1778.

question.leadin: Accused of being a loyalist for voting against the Declaration of Independence, he quickly silenced doubters with his "Declaration...Setting Forth the Causes and Necessities of their Taking Up Arms"
question.text: Name this "Penman of the Revolution" whose wrote a series of letters defending the Constitution under the name Fabius.
question.clue: Along with Thomas McKean, he was one of the two members of the Continental Congress to enter the military, and he opposed John Adams in the Continental Congress by voting against the Declaration of Independence.

swap.leadin: Its namesake wrote a letter to Horatio Gates stating that, "Heaven has been determined to save your country, or a weak general and bad counselors would have ruined it."
swap.text: Name this attempt to remove George Washington from his command of the Continental Army.
swap.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

question.text: Stephen Van Rensselaer married a woman from this family, the daughter of a Revolutionary War general who planned the Saratoga Campaign before he was replaced by Horatio Gates. A woman born to this family discovered the Reynolds Pamphlet while pregnant.
question.answerHtml: Schuyler family [or the Schuylers; accept Peggy Schuyler or Elizabeth Schuyler]

swap.leadin: Name some things about Revolutionary War-era people with a common last name.
swap.text: This British general served as supreme commander of British forces in America from 1778 to 1781, replacing William Howe. He led the army that forced Benjamin Lincoln to surrender Charleston.
swap.clue: While Governor of South Carolina, Rutledge was forced to flee Charleston after the city was attacked and captured by this British general in 1780. He shares his surname with the first governor of New York, who also served as Vice-President under Jefferson and Madison.

question.leadin: This man commissioned William Buckland and William Sears to build his family seat on the Potomac River in 1759.
question.text: Identify this master of Gunston Hall, who drafted the Fairfax Resolves and the Virginia Declaration of Rights, which formed the basis for the United States Bill of Rights.
question.clue: The concepts in this politician's Fairfax Resolves influenced a document he demanded that introduced the right to bear arms.

swap.leadin: Answer three questions related to the career of a certain Virginian.
swap.text: This man, in command of state militia, seized a number of British garrisons in the Ohio and Mississippi valleys as part of the Illinois Campaign of 1778-1779, including Kaskaskia.
swap.clue: POW Leonard Helm delivered Henry Hamilton's surrender to this man after his capture of Fort Sackville.

question.text: St. Leger and Brant were deterred by their unsuccessful siege of this New York fort, which came to an end when they were chased off by Benedict Arnold. This fort also named two treaties between the colonists and the Iroquois in 1768 and 1784.
question.clue: A problem for Burgoyne was the inability of Barry St. Leger's force to take this fort in the Mohawk River Valley, which the British unsuccessfully besieged in August 1777.

swap.leadin: In this battle, the Comte de Grasse's 24 ship west Indies fleet was reinforced after 3 indecisive days with siege guns fron Newport.
swap.text: Name this battle, named the "decisive battle of the war" by Sir William James, lost by Admiral Thomas Graves.
